questions.question: The five aspects a complete development plan must cover are:
options: Economic, social, sustainable, appropriate-scale and spatial development
Mining, farming, tourism, banking and transport
Local, provincial, national, continental and global
Health, wealth, education, sport and culture

questions.question: The Brundtland definition of sustainable development is development that:
options: Maximises this decade's economic output
Meets the needs of the present without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs
Uses only renewable energy sources
Prioritises future generations over present ones

questions.question: Rooftop solar, rainwater tanks and a hand-repairable pump for a remote Wild Coast village illustrate:
options: Spatial development
High mass consumption
Appropriate-scale development — technology matched to local skills, budgets and needs
Backwash effects

questions.question: Social development is described as the conversion step because:
options: It converts imports into exports
It converts rural land into urban land
It converts factories into offices
It turns economic gains into lives — schools, clinics, housing, safe water and the full inclusion of women

questions.question: In the core-periphery model, the backwash effect is:
options: The drain of the periphery's young, skilled people and savings toward the core, leaving the periphery older, poorer and less able to catch up
Investment flowing from the core out to the periphery
The flooding of low-lying coastal cores
The movement of factories from core to periphery

questions.question: Cumulative causation means that:
options: Development spreads itself evenly over time
Success recruits success — each new plant attracts suppliers, workers and taxes that fund the infrastructure which lands the next plant
Peripheries automatically catch up with cores
Causes must be listed in chronological order

questions.question: At the national scale, South Africa's core-periphery pattern is best described as:
options: The coast as core and the interior as periphery
No measurable pattern at all
Gauteng producing roughly a third of GDP on the smallest provincial area as core, with former homeland districts of Limpopo and the Eastern Cape as periphery
Every province holding an equal share of economic activity

questions.question: Most regional development policy amounts to:
options: Moving the core to a new location
Abolishing all peripheries
Encouraging faster backwash
Strengthening spread effects while throttling backwash

questions.question: The correct order of Rostow's five stages is:
options: Traditional society, preconditions for take-off, take-off, drive to maturity, high mass consumption
Take-off, preconditions, maturity, tradition, consumption
High mass consumption, maturity, take-off, preconditions, traditional society
Traditional society, take-off, preconditions, consumption, maturity

questions.question: Take-off is marked by:
options: Subsistence farming reaching its peak
Manufacturing surging while investment climbs past roughly ten per cent of national income, so that growth begins to feed itself
Services overtaking industry as the main employer
The construction of the first railways

questions.question: The criticism that Rostow ignores colonialism argues that:
options: Colonies developed faster than their colonisers
Colonial history is too old to matter
Britain's take-off drew fuel from colonies whose own development was deliberately suppressed, so the ladder was pulled up behind the first climbers
Rostow wrote the model for colonial governments

questions.question: The model's treatment of high mass consumption is criticised because:
options: Consumption is impossible to measure
Most countries skip that stage entirely
Mass consumption arrived before industrialisation historically
It crowns consumption as the summit with no stage for sustainability, never asking whether the planet could carry eight billion mass consumers

subtopics.title: Reading Real Places With Both Models

questions.question: South Africa's preconditions for take-off arrived with:
options: The mineral revolution — railways and harbours built after 1870 to serve diamonds and gold
The arrival of television in the 1970s
The 1994 democratic transition
The construction of shopping malls

questions.question: Apartheid is described as core-periphery engineering written into law because:
options: It abolished the difference between core and periphery
The homelands were designed as labour reservoirs — peripheries whose backwash of migrant workers fed the mining core
It moved the economic core to the homelands
It prevented all migration between regions

questions.question: Post-1994 projects such as the industrial development zones at Saldanha Bay and Richards Bay aim to:
options: Concentrate all industry in Gauteng
Replace manufacturing with subsistence farming
Bolt new cores onto the periphery and pump spread effects outward
Reduce exports through the ports

questions.question: The synthesis of the two models is that:
options: Both models describe the same thing in different words
Core-periphery describes a timeline while Rostow describes a map
Neither model applies to South Africa
Rostow draws a timeline and assumes regions ride it together; core-periphery draws a map and insists they do not — use each for its own kind of question and criticise both

subtopics.title: Five Boxes Every Plan Must Tick

questions.question: In the five-stamps picture, the stamp that asks about TOMORROW checks:
options: Sustainability — building with what can be replaced instead of spending the next generation's inheritance
The size of the project budget
The location of the project
The number of jobs created this year

questions.question: The gleaming high-tech treatment works that nobody local can repair is called a monument because:
options: It is architecturally impressive
It fails the FIT test — without matching local skills and budgets it will stand unused, which is the opposite of appropriate technology
It commemorates the engineers who built it
Monuments attract tourism income

questions.question: The stamp that asks about the MAP checks whether:
options: The plan includes an accurate map of the site
The project is close to a main road
Development is reaching everywhere rather than heaping up in one polished corner
The land has been surveyed

subtopics.title: The Magnet and the Empty Edges

questions.question: In the magnet picture, the iron filings crawling inward represent:
options: Backwash — the periphery's workers, skills and savings drawn toward the core
Spread effects flowing to the periphery
Exports leaving the country
Tourists visiting the coast

questions.question: A mineworker's remittances raising a homestead roof in a Limpopo village is an example of:
options: Backwash
A spread effect — value trickling from core back to periphery
Cumulative causation
Take-off

questions.question: Calling regional planning 'plumbing' means:
options: Water supply is the only development priority
Planners must be qualified artisans
Policy tries to widen the spread pipes and narrow the backwash drain — as the new industrial zones at Richards Bay and Saldanha attempt
Pipelines carry most of the country's freight

questions.question: The full-mark move with the core-periphery model is to:
options: Apply it only at the global scale
Apply it only to South Africa
Avoid mentioning scale at all
Run it at three zoom levels — global North and South, Gauteng and the homeland-era edges, and one metro's office core against its township rim

questions.question: In the aeroplane picture, the ground crew laying rails, dredging harbours and opening banks represents:
options: The preconditions for take-off
Traditional society
The drive to maturity
High mass consumption

questions.question: The plane generating its own lift stands for:
options: Government subsidies replacing private investment
Take-off — growth becoming self-sustaining once manufacturing surges and investment passes about ten per cent of national income
The end of economic growth
A return to subsistence farming

questions.question: 'Some planes fuelled up by draining other planes' tanks' is the criticism that:
options: Air travel is too expensive for poor countries
Rostow underestimated fuel prices
Colonial powers took off partly on resources and markets taken from colonies whose own development was switched off
Modern economies grow faster than older ones

questions.question: South Africa challenges the one-aeroplane model because:
options: The whole economy remains at traditional society
The country reached mass consumption before take-off
Aviation plays no role in the economy
Sections of the economy are cruising while millions were barred from boarding for decades by apartheid — and no stage model has a stage for that
